gap: No result ChatGPT got states that two of its three picks show as not buyable on their makers' US stores today (2026-11-13). J-Tech Digital's store returns the JTECH-14EX60-AE ($302.49) with available=false, and OREI's store shows the UHD12-EX115-K ($139.99) as 'Unavailable'.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited OREI support articles (UHD12-EX115-K, UHD14-EXB400-K). They cover specs and limits in depth: distance per resolution, PoC, EDID presets, IR, the 'duplicates one source' limit and no 4K120. They give no price and no stock status. None of the other ten OREI support results mention price or stock either. ChatGPT's prices came from catalog cards, not from any result page.
decides: This weakens ChatGPT's 'Best overall 1x4' (J-Tech) and 'Best for 2 TVs' (OREI UHD12-EX115-K) picks, because neither is buyable from its maker today. The page should name a buyable alternative for each slot or point to the retailer that has stock. I could not confirm the price or stock of the remaining pick, the OREI UHD14-EXB400-K, on a page I opened, so this finding does not confirm it as the fallback. Our only listed product in this space, the AV Access 4KEX70-H2, is a 1x1 extender and cannot fill a splitter slot.

findings.label: Maker-stated reach and features

findings.source_title: 4K 60Hz 1x4 HDMI Extender Splitter Over Ethernet w/ Audio Extraction, PoC, 4K Downscaling
findings.note: Taken from the product description text in the store JSON. The maker text does not say whether 196 ft applies at 4K60 or only at 1080p.

findings.note: Page fetched. The price area reads 'Unavailable' and there is no compare-at price. An 'Add to cart' label is also present, so the out-of-stock reading is likely but not certain. Re-check before publishing.

findings.label: Where it loses: 4K60 reach
findings.value: 4K@60Hz up to 115 ft (35 m); 4K@30Hz 164 ft (50 m); 1080p60 197 ft (60 m) over Cat6/6a/7; 2 receivers, max power 8.28 W
findings.source_title: UHD12-EX115-K Overview and Use Cases – OREI
findings.note: Reach is the shortest of ChatGPT's three picks at 4K60, and it has only 2 outputs. A cited rival page already states this.

findings.label: Where it wins and loses: reach vs power draw
findings.value: 4K@60Hz up to 394 ft (120 m), 1080p60 492 ft (150 m), HDBaseT, 4 receivers, RS-232 pass-through; transmitter draws 35 W on a 24 V/2.7 A adapter
findings.source_title: UHD14-EXB400-K Overview and Use Cases – OREI
findings.note: Longest reach of the three picks. It loses on price ($429 per ChatGPT's card; see unsourced) and power draw. A cited rival page already states the specs.

findings.label: Price and why it loses (our product)
findings.value: $156.72 sale (regular $164.99); 1x1 point-to-point kit, not a splitter; 4K60 4:4:4 up to 131 ft (40 m) over Cat6a/7, 115 ft over Cat5e/6; 1080p 230 ft (70 m)
findings.source_title: 4K HDBaseT Extender HDMI 2.0 up to 70m, Supports HDCP2.2, HDR10, 2-Way IR, PoE & RS232
findings.note: The page states that one transmitter works with only one receiver, so it cannot feed 2 or 4 TVs on its own. That disqualifies it for a splitter question. Stock was not stated explicitly; an Add to cart button was present.
